title.en: Waste management: sewage, solid waste and e-waste

text.en: Every day we throw away plastics, food scraps, old phones and dirty water. Managing this waste decides the health of our soil, rivers and air.

Sewage is wastewater from homes and industries (dye, textile, leather, sugar, paper); untreated sewage is the leading polluter of water sources in India.
Sewage treatment: pre-screening, aeration, sedimentation and sludge removal, disinfection by chlorine or UV, and reuse.
Solid waste (municipal, hospital, industrial, e-waste) is managed by segregation, sanitary landfill, incineration and composting.
Composting turns biodegradable waste into humus using microbes or earthworms; incineration burns non-biodegradable medical waste.
The 4R approach is Reduce, Reuse, Recover and Recycle; paper, bagasse, paddy husk and cowdung are recycled or reused.
E-waste is discarded electronic equipment (computers, phones, appliances, batteries) holding lead, cadmium, chromium and mercury.
Computers make 66 percent of e-waste and only 5 percent of e-waste is recycled.
Health effects: lead harms the nervous system, cadmium accumulates in kidney and liver, mercury damages brain and lungs and burning PVC releases dioxin.

problem.en: Why must biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes be segregated?

text.en: Biodegradable waste can be composted into manure.
Non-biodegradable waste like plastic needs recycling or special disposal.
Mixing them spoils compost and pollutes soil, so segregation is the first step.

prompt.en: Describe the steps in sewage treatment.

points.en: Sewage treatment: screening, aeration, sedimentation, disinfection.
